title: Pointwise Competing-Risk CATE Rates in a Two-Visit Experiment with Balanced Smoothness
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < ceiling_for_field 7.4; salvageable=false within the fixed-K=2 known-uniform-design scope.
gap_reasons: The contribution is therefore a genuine sharp minimax phase diagram but remains tied to a narrow benchmark experiment with known smoothness indices and strong fixed positivity, limiting its significance for a leading general econometrics journal.

The projected score is further constrained by the absence of numerical evidence demonstrating finite-sample behavior or the practical size of the claimed resolution improvement for individualized CIF estimation.

positioning_incomplete@thm:balanced-cubic-frontier: The computable matched-rate theorem is a genuine Stat contribution on its stated K=2 class, but its theorem-level positioning and several related-work comparisons are incomplete.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery built a matched cubic, quadratic, and saturation phase diagram for a fixed K=2, known-uniform-design competing-risk model. D0.5 judged the contribution subfield rather than the required field tier and not salvageable within this scope. Its small-cube proof gap was repaired and independently cleared before banking; theorem-level prior-work positioning and finite-sample evidence remain open.
tldr: For the fixed two-visit, known-uniform, fourteen-cell competing-risk experiment, the pointwise minimax expected absolute-error risk over the complete balanced range \(0<s\leq\gamma\) is \(n^{-\min\{4s\gamma/(4s\gamma+2sd+d\gamma),\,\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\}}\). A denominator-safe observed-data cubic estimator attains the first phase through \(s_3=d\gamma/(4\gamma+6d)\); a quadratic estimator takes over above \(s_3\), and the rate saturates at the ordinary pointwise exponent at \(s_*=d\gamma/(4\gamma+2d)\). Matching lower bounds use the full fourteen-cell correlated-sign experiment below \(s_*\) and a localized full-history two-point experiment at and above it.
gap: Uncensored Hölder CATE has matched minimax theory, while competing-risk CATE has identification, learner bounds, forests, and first-order inference; none of the inspected sources states a matched pointwise rate for the same censored full-history class in the strict cubic-active region.
fill: A projected multinomial pilot controls denominator sums, separate quadratic and cubic grids balance Taylor bias against each Hoeffding order, and a full-history correlated-sign experiment matches the resulting exponent.
